The raise escapes run_suite_fixtures before save_eval_report is reached (run.py:89-99), and the endpoint catches only KeyError (main.py:2790-2793), so it 500s, no report row exists and the other N-1 graded trials are discarded. Verified, with two line corrections: "emi" is graders.py:209 and "due" is :211 (tuple opens at :201). All three consumers use bare substring membership over a lower-cased join with no word boundary: graders.py:256 (`w in script`, voicemail), :276 (`w in said`, third party) and :393 (`w in first`, outbound opening). "emi" is a substring of "reminder"/"remind", so a compliant callback voicemail fails grade_voicemail_discloses_nothing with the detail "voicemail names emi" (:262-263), a word the operator never wrote. Latent only because the shipped fixtures avoid it (fixtures.py PUBLISH_OUTBOUND_TASKS) — the trap fires on any author-supplied voicemail_script or opening turn.

The precedence claim is arithmetically right but the defect is not established, and one supporting claim is false. graders.py:394 is a SINGLE physical line — `asks_why = "how can i help" in first or "what can i" in first or "calling about" in first and "?" in first` — not three stacked siblings, so the "layout reads as three sibling phrases" argument does not exist in the file. On intent, the grader's contract is explicitly about ASKING, not stating: the docstring says it catches "an outbound call that opens by *asking* why they are calling" (graders.py:381-384) and the failure detail is "outbound call opened by asking the borrower why we called" (graders.py:401). Under that contract the "?"-conditional third clause is coherent — it targets "…what are you calling about?", the inbound script — while a declarative "calling about …" is the normal outbound behaviour and is still policed by the separate confirms check (:392) and the _DEBT_WORDS leak check (:393). The only test in the repo for this grader exercises "how can I help you today?" (tests/test_outbound_conduct.py:358-364) and asserts nothing about "calling about". What would settle it: a fixture, ADR or test asserting that a declarative "calling about" opening must fail; absent that, this is a style observation, not wrong runtime behaviour.
